feature: An alignment guide across level buttons reads aligned
summary: A guide drawn along the tops of a bordered button and a filled button now reads Top edges aligned with one item per button. Before, the bordered button was read three times (its border has an inner side that stops short of the rounded corners) and the check said off 1 px with 4 items. The tolerance in the Experiments window is now in points, so a single device pixel of wobble on a Retina capture no longer counts.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. next-measure-align is on by default, tolerance 1. Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png.

try.do: Press I for Measure and set the mode to Alignment.
Drag a guide from left to right along the tops of the Reset and Save Changes buttons, starting a little left of Reset, then release.
Read the chip: Top edges aligned. The Measurements row should say Top edges, 2 items.
Undo, then press the guide's start a few pixels lower, inside the Reset button's border, and drag again. It should still read aligned with 2 items.
Drag a guide straight down just left of the three labels in the second card. It should still read Left edges, off 4 px, unchanged.
Open Experiments, set Alignment tolerance to 0, and repeat the button guide. It should now report the sub-point difference between the two buttons.

evaluate: When the guide settles on the buttons' shared top, does it sit where your eye says the tops are, or a pixel in from the bordered button's outline?
Is 1 point the right default tolerance for a Retina capture, or should a redliner see anything over half a point?
Would you want the chip to say how many items it checked (Top edges aligned, 2 items), or is the Measurements row enough?
rough: A guide that runs only along the straight part of a bordered button, never crossing a corner, sees the border's two sides at equal length and falls back to whichever is nearer the drawn line. Across two buttons a guide always crosses a corner, so this did not come up.

On a 2x capture a guide along the tops of small labels may now settle on the x-height line rather than the cap line when the two are 4 device px apart, the same way it already does on 1x captures. Both labels get the same treatment, so the verdict holds.
